name: Highborne
summary: Across the ancient Kaldorei Empire, the Highborne wielded the Well of Eternity for Queen Azshara. Their sorcery drew the Burning Legion to Azeroth, unleashing the War of the Ancients and the Great Sundering.

sections.title: Aristocrats of the Well
sections.body:
Before the Sundering, the Highborne rose around Queen Azshara as the favored upper class. They claimed superiority over common kaldorei through selective bloodlines and intelligence. Opulent privilege set them apart, and they kept tight control of the Well of Eternity.

There they learned to shape its primal arcane power. Across ancient Kalimdor, they raised magnificent cities. Their hunger for sorcery drove them to draw ever more deeply from the Well, until its calm waters grew turbulent and dark.

sections.title: The Betrayal and the Sundering
sections.body:
The Highborne’s spellcraft drew the attention of the dark titan Sargeras and the Burning Legion. Azshara and her counselor Xavius persuaded the Highborne that demons would remake the world as an untainted paradise.

The Highborne opened a massive gateway inside the Well of Eternity, unleashing the War of the Ancients. Demonic hordes slaughtered the populace, while rebels rallied by Malfurion Stormrage fought to close the portal. Then the Well imploded and tore the supercontinent apart.

sections.title: Scattered Heirs and Remnants
sections.body:
After the Sundering, the Highborne met different fates. Those dragged beneath the waves with Azshara were twisted into serpentine naga. Others fell to demonic curses and became satyrs. Dath'Remar Sunstrider led a faction that aided the resistance but refused to give up arcane magic.

Exiled across the sea, they founded the high elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. Today, isolated enclaves such as the Shen'dralar remain cloistered in Eldre'Thalas, shunned remnants of an empire that nearly destroyed Azeroth.

faq.answer: In Darnassian, the Highborne were called the quel'dorei, meaning “children of noble birth.” They chose that name for their aristocratic bloodlines and magical aptitude, setting themselves apart from the rest of kaldorei society.

faq.q: Are modern night elves related to the Highborne?
aliases: difference between night elves and highborne
faq.answer: Yes. The Highborne were the noble, magic-wielding ruling caste of the ancient night elves. They were physically the same race, though slightly paler and prone to flamboyant dress. After the Sundering, night elf society banned arcane magic and abolished the caste.

faq.q: How did the Highborne cause the War of the Ancients?
faq.answer: The Highborne’s unchecked use of the Well of Eternity sent magical ripples across the cosmos and attracted the Burning Legion. Enticed by Sargeras’s promises of unmatched power and an idealized world, Azshara and her nobles channeled the Well to open a portal. The demon army then entered Kalimdor.

faq.q: Did all Highborne side with Queen Azshara?
faq.answer: No. Several factions broke away when they saw the demonic devastation. Sorcerers led by Dath'Remar Sunstrider joined Malfurion's Kaldorei Resistance. Groups such as the Shen'dralar in Eldre'Thalas focused on surviving and defending their regional holdings.

faq.q: What happened to the surviving Highborne after the war?
faq.answer: The Highborne lineage scattered into several fates. Many who sank with Zin-Azshari became naga, while others were twisted into satyrs. Those who followed Dath'Remar were exiled to the Eastern Kingdoms and became high elves. A few, including the Shen'dralar in Dire Maul, remained cloistered in ancient ruins.

The Shen'dralar are an ancient sect of Highborne scholars and arcanists who defended Eldre'Thalas, the southern city, during the Great Sundering. Cut off from Queen Azshara and mainstream kaldorei society, they retreated into the city, now called Dire Maul. There they relied on dark sorceries to preserve their immortality.

angles.text: The Highborne caste remains a deep scar in night elven memory. After the Sundering, arcane magic was outlawed across Kalimdor under pain of exile or death.
The Highborne were the first mortal practitioners of arcane magic on Azeroth. Their breathtaking achievements and catastrophic mistakes shaped the dangerous rules of modern spellcasting.
Druidism arose as a natural philosophy against the Highborne’s reckless exploitation of the Well of Eternity. It laid the foundation for healing Kalimdor after the empire fell.
The Highborne were the first mortals on Azeroth to treat with the Burning Legion. They bartered cosmic secrets and made demonic pacts that paved the way for modern fel studies.
